rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday choice for letting someone escape harm or punishment.

example.english: Please spare me this time; I definitely won't dare do it again next time.
example.traditional: 今次你放過我，下次我一定唔敢喇。
example.jyutping: gam1 ci3 nei5 fong3 gwo3 ngo5 haa6 ci3 ngo5 jat1 ding6 m4 gam2 laa3

rows.note: Use this when stressing mercy or leniency, especially instead of punishing or dealing harshly with someone.

example.english: Please spare the beginner; don't beat them into surrender as soon as the game starts.
example.traditional: 對住新手你就手下留情啦，唔好一開波就打到佢投降。
example.jyutping: deoi3 zyu6 san1 sau2 nei5 zau6 sau2 haa6 lau4 cing4 laa1 m4 hou2 jat1 hoi1 bo1 zau6 daa2 dou3 keoi5 tau4 hong4

rows.note: Use this specifically when asking or ordering someone to spare a person's life, often in dramatic or playful language.

example.english: Spare my life, boss! I only took a piece of candy!
example.traditional: 大佬饒命呀，我只係攞咗粒糖啫！
example.jyutping: daai6 lou2 jiu4 meng6 aa3 ngo5 zi2 hai6 lo2 zo2 nap1 tong4 ze1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for something extra, unnecessary, or not wanted, such as 多餘時間.

example.english: You don't need to buy so much; these are spare.
example.traditional: 你唔使買咁多，呢啲係多餘嘅。
example.jyutping: nei5 m4 sai2 maai5 gam3 do1 ni1 di1 hai6 do1 jyu4 ge3

rows.note: Use this for an item kept ready as a backup, such as a 後備車匙 or 後備輪胎.

example.english: I have a spare tire in the trunk.
example.jyutping: ngo5 ce1 mei5 soeng1 jau5 tiu4 hau6 bei6 taai5

rows.note: Use this mainly for a spare room or other unoccupied space that is available for use.

example.english: There is a spare room upstairs that you can stay in.
example.traditional: 樓上仲有間空房，可以畀你住。
example.jyutping: lau4 soeng6 zung6 jau5 gaan1 hung1 fong2 ho2 ji5 bei2 nei5 zyu6
